title: Block explorer logs (${env})
description: CloudWatch Logs Insights over the ECS task and WAF log groups. Auto-refresh is off by default: Insights bills on bytes scanned, and the WAF group alone is a few hundred MB an hour. Terraform owns this dashboard, so edits made here are replaced on the next apply.

list.name: container
list.label: Container
list.description: Which container's stream to read. The app writes under frontend/, the ADOT metrics sidecar under adot-sidecar/.

list.name: filter
list.label: Filter (regex, case-insensitive)
list.description: Applied to the raw log line on both the app and WAF panels. Empty matches everything.

list.name: outcome
list.label: WAF outcome
list.description: ALLOW is a request a soaking rule matched and the ACL served anyway. BLOCK is a request the ACL rejected.

panels.title: Log lines per interval
panels.description: Honours the container and filter pickers, so with a filter set this is the rate of matching lines — the fastest way to place a burst before reading it.

targets.expression:
filter @logStream like /^($${container:pipe})\//
| filter @message like /(?i)$${filter:raw}/
| stats count(*) as lines by bin($__interval)

panels.title: Logs — $container
panels.description: The app has no log levels: Next.js and the console calls under lib/ write unstructured lines to stdout, and a multi-line dump such as a Zod parse failure arrives as one event per line. Search with the filter box rather than expecting a level field.

targets.expression:
fields @timestamp, @message, @logStream
| filter @logStream like /^($${container:pipe})\//
| filter @message like /(?i)$${filter:raw}/
| sort @timestamp desc, @ptr desc
| limit 500

panels.title: Count-mode matches by rule and country
panels.description: Requests a managed group flagged while soaking, all of them served. One hosting region dominating the table is the ordinary reading: the anonymous-IP list matches datacenter and VPN egress, which is where crawlers and wallet backends live.

targets.expression:
fields nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId as rule, httpRequest.country as country
| filter ispresent(rule)
| stats count(*) as matches by rule, country
| sort matches desc
| limit 25

panels.title: Count-mode matches by client IP
panels.description: A single IP taking most of the table means the count volume is one client, not broad hostile traffic — worth a reverse lookup before reading anything into the totals.

targets.expression:
fields nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId as rule, httpRequest.clientIp as clientIp, httpRequest.country as country
| filter ispresent(rule)
| stats count(*) as matches by clientIp, country, rule
| sort matches desc
| limit 25

panels.title: Count-mode matches by URI
panels.description: Explorer routes here mean real users behind a flagged IP range. Probe paths — wp-login, .env, phpmyadmin — mean the rule is earning its place.

targets.expression:
fields nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId as rule, httpRequest.uri as uri
| filter ispresent(rule)
| stats count(*) as matches by uri
| sort matches desc
| limit 25

panels.title: WAF events — $outcome
panels.description: The log group holds only requests a rule matched: the delivery filter drops everything else, so this is not a request log. action ALLOW next to a populated countMatchedRule is the shape to expect while waf_managed_rules_blocking is off — the rule matched, the ACL fell through to its default allow, and the request was served. action BLOCK with terminatingRuleId set is a real rejection.

targets.expression:
fields @timestamp, action, terminatingRuleId, nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId as countMatchedRule, httpRequest.country as country, httpRequest.clientIp as clientIp, httpRequest.httpMethod as method, httpRequest.uri as uri
| filter action like /^($${outcome:pipe})$/
| filter @message like /(?i)$${filter:raw}/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
